sections.title: The letter Y
paragraphs: The letter (Y) /ɪ/ makes the sound /j/, as in (yes) /jɛs/, which means yes. This letter makes four different sounds in English. Sometimes it works as a consonant, and sometimes it works as a vowel.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Raise the middle of your tongue close to the roof of your mouth. Let voiced air glide through smoothly. For the second sound, smile slightly and keep your tongue high at the front. For the third sound, open your mouth wide, then glide up to a smile. For the last sound, relax your tongue slightly lower. Touch your throat to feel your voice buzz.

sections.title: Reading and spelling
paragraphs: At the start of a word before a vowel, it sounds like /j/, as in (yard) /jɑːd/. Unstressed at the end of a word, it sounds like /i/, as in (happy) /hæ.pi/. At the end of a short word or in an open stressed syllable, it sounds like /aɪ/, as in (my) /maɪ/. Inside a closed syllable, it sounds like /ɪ/, as in (gym) /dʒɪm/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not turn the first sound into a hard friction sound like the start of judge. Keep the airflow smooth and open. Do not lengthen the short vowel sound into a long tense vowel. Keep your tongue relaxed and slightly low.
